answer: Require a stake that grows with every new identity. An agent locks a deposit into a shared kernel of reputation, and the deposit is slashed if it cheats. A bad actor can spin up many fake agents, but each one costs real money, so flooding the network gets expensive fast. Think of the stake as an ember that stays lit only while the agent behaves: trust builds slowly and burns away in one bad move. Honest agents carry a cipher of signed history, and peers check it before trading, so a fresh fake has nothing to show and gets ignored.
